newsitem.title: USA: Carson Pirie Feb same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: Carson Pirie Feb same store sales up.

text.p: Carson Pirie Scott & Co said Monday its same-store sales rose 8.2 percent in February while total sales in the month were up 13.2 percent.

"I am upbeat about our prospects for the upcoming (fiscal) year," Chairman Stanton Bluestone said in a statement. "I am particularly encouraged by our strong start in the month of February, during which were recorded (an) 8.2 percent comparable store sales increase and a 13.2 percent total sales increase."

Earlier, Carson reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended February 1 of $1.73 a share, up from $1.40 a year ago. The year-ago quarter included $0.25 a share in acquisition costs as well as $0.04 a share in gains.
For the year, it earned $2.39 a share, which included a $0.54 gain from the sale of Profitt's Inc stock, a $0.38 writedown of County Seat, a $0.09 charitable contribution and a $0.01 other charge.
Year-ago earnings were $3.75 a share, which included a $1.92 a share gain on the sale of Minnesota stores, $0.24 in acquisition costs and a $0.03 gain.
The company said its same-store sales were up 2.2 percent for the year, led by 15 percent improvements in special sizes and outerwear.

During 1996, Carson said, it reduced its net debt to capital ratio to 28 percent from 32 percent a year ago. This reduction was despite cash uses of $12.3 million for share repurchases and $52.9 million for capital expenditures, it added.
During the fourth quarter, Carson repurchased 50,900 shares of its common stock for $1.2 million. During fiscal 1996, it repurchased 517,000 shares, or three percent of shares outstanding.
